w: Construction began under Haile Selassie in 1931, stalled through the Italian occupation, and finished in 1942 as a monument to Ethiopia's victory over it. The highest-ranking Ethiopian Orthodox cathedral in the capital, it has also become a resting place for the country's most prominent dead.
s: Built to celebrate victory over Italian occupation
_facts: Initially built 1931 under Haile Selassie, disrupted by Italian invasion, completed 1942
Built to commemorate the Ethiopian victory over Italian occupation
Highest-ranking Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo cathedral in Addis Ababa
Noted burial place of prominent Ethiopians

w: Haile Selassie lived here until the 1974 coup ended his reign; the Derg government that followed turned it into the official residence of Ethiopia's head of state, a role it still holds. Same address, same walls, an entirely different Ethiopia on the other side of the gate.
s: From emperor's home to president's residence
_facts: Formerly Eyubelyu (Jubilee) Palace, house of Emperor Haile Selassie until the 1974 coup
Official residence of the President of Ethiopia since the Derg government

w: Merkato takes its name straight from the Italian word for market, a legacy of the occupation years - and it grew so large that the surrounding district simply took the market's name too. One of the continent's biggest open-air markets, still trading under a borrowed word.
s: An Italian word that swallowed a whole district
_facts: Name Merkato comes from the Italian word for market
Large open-air marketplace in the Addis Ketema district
The neighborhood takes its name from the market

w: Mengistu Haile Mariam raised this fifty-metre memorial to the Ethiopian and Cuban dead of the Ogaden War, with wall reliefs and portrait squares for the Cuban soldiers. Some of its sculptures arrived as a 1984 gift from North Korea - one of Pyongyang's first monument donations to Africa.
s: A Cold War memorial, gifted partly by North Korea
_facts: Memorial to Ethiopian and Cuban soldiers of the Ogaden War, built under Mengistu Haile Mariam
50-metre pillar with wall reliefs and portrait squares of Cuban soldiers
Some sculptures donated by North Korea in 1984, one of its first monument donations to Africa

n: National Archives and Library of Ethiopia
w: Haile Selassie inaugurated Ethiopia's national library and archive in 1944, seeding its first shelves with books from his own collection. Eight decades on it is still the country's official keeper of record - a monarch's personal donation grown into a national institution.
s: Opened in 1944 on the emperor's own book donation
_facts: Inaugurated 1944 by Emperor Haile Selassie
Began service with books donated by the emperor

w: This obelisk in the middle of Sidist Kilo's roundabout marks the Yekatit 12 pogrom - three days in February 1937 when occupying Italian forces carried out a massacre in the city, an atrocity remembered here by its date on the Ethiopian calendar rather than a Western one.
s: An obelisk marking a three-day massacre
_facts: Memorial to the Yekatit 12 pogrom, an Italian war crime committed 19-21 February 1937
An obelisk at the centre of Sidist Kilo Square, also called Yekatit 12 Square

w: Ethiopia's first university museum, tucked inside Addis Ababa University's main campus alongside the Institute of Ethiopian Studies. Its cabinets run from musical instruments to anthropological artefacts - a working research collection as much as a public one, built by scholars rather than curators.
_facts: First university museum in Ethiopia
Houses anthropological, musicological and cultural objects
Located on Addis Ababa University's main campus with the Institute of Ethiopian Studies

w: Italian occupiers built this as Cinema Marconi, a modest 250-seat picture house. Haile Selassie relaunched it as the national theatre in 1955, installing an Austrian composer, Franz Zelwecker, as its first director general - a cinema turned into the country's premier stage, occupation-era bricks and all.
s: Built by occupying Italians as a 250-seat cinema
_facts: Originally built by Italians during occupation as Cinema Marconi, about 250 seats
Established as national theatre in 1955 under Haile Selassie, formerly Haile Selassie I Theater
Austrian composer Franz Zelwecker was its first director general

w: Haile Selassie wanted a building that would shame Ethiopia's wealthy into investing in their own capital rather than hoarding money 'under the mattress' - so this UN Economic Commission for Africa headquarters went up in just 18 months, completed in 1961, built almost entirely from home-produced materials.
s: Built in 18 months to prove a point about self-reliance
_facts: Permanent headquarters of the UN Economic Commission for Africa, completed February 1961 in 18 months
Haile Selassie wanted it built with home-produced materials to encourage local investment
A UN-funded 1971-1975 extension added 130,000 square metres

n: Ethiopia Museum of Art and Science
w: Opened by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed in 2022 as part of a Chinese-aided riverside redevelopment, this science museum takes the shape of a nine-metre circular 'ring of wisdom.' Inside: a dome theatre for 3D films and interactive halls on robotics, cybersecurity and data.
s: A 'ring of wisdom' built for the digital era
_facts: Inaugurated by PM Abiy Ahmed in October 2022, part of the Addis Ababa Riverside Development Project
9-metre circular shape dubbed the 'ring of wisdom'
Includes a Dome Theatre for 3D films and interactive displays on robotics, cybersecurity and GIS

w: Everyone calls it Arat Kilo, but its formal name marks a single date doing double duty: 27 Miyazya, the day Addis Ababa fell to Italy in 1936 and, five years later, the day it was liberated. The square it names is ringed by the Ministry of Education, Addis Ababa University and Holy Trinity Cathedral.
s: One date marks both the fall and the liberation
_facts: Name marks 27 Miyazya (5 May), the day Addis Ababa fell to Italy in 1936 and was liberated in 1941
Commonly called Arat Kilo
Surrounded by government buildings and Addis Ababa University, near Holy Trinity Cathedral

w: Curator Meskerem Assegued built this environmentally conscious artist residency into one of the main conduits linking Ethiopian visual artists to European and American galleries. A sister site sits in Harla, near Dire Dawa - two outposts of the same idea, run on locally sourced, sustainable construction.
s: An eco-built residency that put Ethiopian art abroad
_facts: Formerly Zoma Contemporary Art Center, environmentally conscious artist-in-residency project
Influential conduit linking Ethiopian artists to European and American galleries
Second location in Harla, near Dire Dawa
Headed by curator Meskerem Assegued

w: Ethiopia's national museum sits near Addis Ababa University's graduate school in the heart of the capital - the country's flagship repository, gathering its collections under one roof a short walk from where much of that history keeps getting studied and re-examined by scholars next door.
_facts: National museum of Ethiopia
Located near Addis Ababa University's graduate school

w: Distinctive for its octagonal form, this Ethiopian Orthodox cathedral anchors the northern end of Churchill Road - a geometric departure from the domed and cross-shaped churches around it, instantly recognisable against the capital's skyline.
s: An octagonal cathedral on Churchill Road
_facts: Ethiopian Orthodox church noted for its distinctive octagonal form
Located at the northern end of Churchill Road

w: The highest point of the Entoto range, rising 3,200 metres above sea level and looking straight down over the entire sprawl of Addis Ababa below - the mountain the capital was practically built in the shadow of.
s: 3,200 metres, looking down on the whole capital
_facts: Highest peak of the Entoto Mountains, 3,200 metres above sea level
Overlooks the city of Addis Ababa
